args.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(beadrs-3be01f97): build claim --why trace from pre-claim eligibility snapshot

The hidden second claim itself was already removed in 6662c31 (cmd_claim
now calls the read-only trace builder instead of claim_issue_with_trace),
but the trace was still assembled from post-mutation state, so a
successful 'claim --why' contradicted itself: selected_factors described
the just-claimed bead as in_progress/assigned/ineligible, and the
eligibility summary counted it under already_assigned/not_open_status.

Split the trace assembly out of create_decision_trace:

- collect_eligibility_factors is now public and read-only; callers inside
  a write transaction snapshot it before mutating
- new build_decision_trace(factors, selected, assignee) assembles the
  trace from a snapshot, so it explains the decision as it was made
- cmd_claim snapshots factors before the claim (both FIFO and --policy
  paths share this code) and assembles the trace afterwards from the bead
  the claim actually selected
- claim_issue_with_trace (library API) snapshots the same way

Regression test test_claim_with_why_claims_exactly_one_issue asserts,
over a fresh workspace with three ready beads, that 'claim --why' leaves
exactly one in_progress issue, decision_trace.selected_issue_id equals
claim_result.bead_id, and selected_factors shows decision-time state
(open, unassigned, eligible).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1

content:
Done. Bead `beadrs-3be01f97` closed, both commits pushed to `origin/main`.

## What I found

The headline bug was **already half-fixed at HEAD**: commit `6662c31` (beadrs-b412cc80, landed earlier today) had replaced `cmd_claim`'s `claim_issue_with_trace` call with the read-only `create_decision_trace`, so acceptance criteria 1 (exactly one `in_progress`) and 2 (`selected_issue_id == claim_result.bead_id`) already passed — I verified both live before touching anything.

What remained was the other half of the reproduced bug: the trace was still assembled **after** the mutation, so `selected_factors` described the just-claimed bead as `in_progress`/`assigned`/`ineligible` while `reasons` said `eligible_selected`, and the summary counted phantom `already_assigned`/`not_open_status` ineligibilities.

## The fix (`3f720bb`)

- Split `create_decision_trace` in `src/service/claim.rs` into a public read-only `collect_eligibility_factors` plus a new `build_decision_trace(factors, selected, assignee)`
- `cmd_claim` (`src/main.rs:120-180`) now snapshots factors **before** the claim (FIFO and `--policy` paths share this code) and assembles the trace afterwards against the bead the claim actually selected
- `claim_issue_with_trace` (the library API named in the bug report) snapshots the same way
- Regression test `test_claim_with_why_claims_exactly_one_issue` in `tests/r001_decision_traces.rs`: 3 ready beads, one `claim --why`, asserts exactly one `in_progress`, ID equality, and decision-time `selected_factors`

## Verification

- Live repro on both `fifo-v1` and `aging-v1` paths: one `in_progress`, IDs match, `selected_factors` now `open`/`unassigned`/`eligible`
- `cargo fmt` clean, `clippy --all-targets` clean, full `cargo test` green (38/38 test binaries, exit 0)
